an initial dataset of 8,980 images is compiled. Following a data cleaning phase, 8,895 images are retained for annotation.
After the second round of annotation and final quality control measures, the final dataset comprises 8,794 images and 28,607 QA pairs.
Approximately 30% of the overall image data is obtained from public datasets, with 20% sourced from the web and 50% from manual collection, respectively.
A total of 1,220 images from document scenarios and 876 images from natural scenarios are collected for the test set of the MTVQA benchmark.
Image acquisition costs about two months and 30,000 dollars. VQA annotation costs about three months and 60,000 dollars.

the annotation team is divided into two independent groups. One group is tasked with generating questions and providing answers based on the images, while the other group is responsible for evaluating and correcting the QA pairs.
The annotators must be native speakers of the corresponding language and have actively utilized it for a minimum duration of 10 years.
the annotation results for each language underwent a 10% sampling inspection by a quality inspector to ensure adherence to standards.
